record.what_it_does: AI search engine over peer-reviewed papers, with a cited-answer research agent.
record.auth_notes: REST API: the API key goes in an x-api-key header. consensus.app/home/mcp shows a curl example with -H "x-api-key: $CONSENSUS_API_KEY". Hosted MCP (https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp): the user either signs in with OAuth or sends the API key as "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY", according to the Consensus-NLP/consensus-mcp README. The README doesn't mention DCR, and no primary source confirms it. I found no documented OAuth for the REST API, so OAuth exists only on the MCP server. Each API key belongs to one user, so a multi-user toolkit would collect each user's key or go through MCP OAuth.
record.access_notes: The REST API page says API access is "Included on every paid plan". Paid plans are Pro, Deep, Team and Enterprise. consensus.app/.well-known/pricing.md is less generous: it lists the Search API only under Team ("Optional access ... available upon approval, rate limited") and Enterprise (custom pricing). The two sources conflict on whether approval is needed. MCP is more open. Its search tool works with no account at 3 papers per search. The Free plan gets 10 papers per search and 30 calls a month, without DOI or full-text fields. Pro/Teams get 500 calls a month, Deep 2,000, and Enterprise custom limits. Paid plans can turn on extra usage at $0.05 per call.
record.api_breadth_notes: REST has two main endpoints: GET /v1/search, which returns ranked papers, and POST /v1/threads, which starts an async research agent run in Pro or Deep mode. The MCP server exposes five tools: search, create_thread, get_thread, add_to_thread and find_threads. Filters include study design, sample size, journal quartile and year.
record.mcp_notes: The hosted server is at https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp and supports OAuth sign-in or a Bearer API key. The repo is github.com/Consensus-NLP/consensus-mcp and the setup guide is at docs.consensus.app/consensus-mcp. The MCP search tool works without an account, and a free tier allows 30 calls a month.
record.blocker_notes: REST access needs a paid plan, and one Consensus page says Team access is "available upon approval". The API surface is small. The OAuth the request asked for is available only on the MCP server, not the REST API. A toolkit could use REST with each user's own API key, or wrap the official remote MCP over OAuth, which also covers free and no-account users with limits. The docs site (docs.consensus.app) returns 403 to automated fetches.
